steps.title: Start with what the camera saw.
steps.description: Track the person through the clip. Keep the joint estimates, confidence and gaps so the reconstruction can be checked against its source.

steps.title: Give the movement a body.
steps.description: Build an articulated skeleton with joint limits and a ground plane. The result can run in a physics engine; depth and contact remain model assumptions.

steps.title: Decide what a good result means.
steps.description: Attach a tracking task before running the controller. Fixed scoring rules make it possible to compare results without moving the goalposts.

steps.title: Run it. Keep the result.
steps.description: An assisted reference controller follows the observed motion. Save the outcome and the recording, including the checks that passed or failed. This is programmed control, not a learned policy.

steps.title: Change the character, not the experiment.
steps.description: A generated panda takes the place of the robot during the recording. The simulated body, controller and score continue unchanged. The video above is the excerpt after that swap.
